approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Apple TV TVML text can be styled with predefined tv-text-style values, font weights and families, and inline bold, italic, or strikethrough tags.
Rock Apple TV media commands can play video from MP4 or HLS sources and audio from MP3 sources, but they cannot play YouTube content.

Rock Apple TV documentation groups JavaScript command behavior as a core part of building TV applications, so TV app guidance should treat commands as part of navigation, media, utility, and demo workflows.

notes: Read-only source inspection verified Rock TV app templates use rockCommand attributes for navigation, login/logout, and media playback commands with command-specific parameters.
This confirms the command surface exists in local TV app implementation examples; agents still need to verify the exact current TV app/page template being edited.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: A Rock Apple TV app is created as a Rock-managed TV application record under CMS configuration, with Rock-side settings that are distinct from the App Store name.

notes: Read-only SQL verified TV Application List, Apple TV Application Detail, Apple TV Page Detail, and TV Page List admin blocks, plus a TV Site record with SiteType 2, page-view tracking, default page, and login page.

Source evidence shows Apple TV application settings are edited and stored in Rock-side Site/additional-settings surfaces, including app JavaScript, styles, API key, authentication page, and interaction retention.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Rock's Lava API guidance identifies Apple TV and Roku channels as examples of custom APIs that can be built with Lava, but warns that Lava webhooks do not include security by default.

notes: Read-only source inspection verified the Lava webhook handler matches active defined values by URL/method, reads Template and EnabledLavaCommands, and renders Lava without an explicit permission check in the inspected handler path.

The Apple TV/Roku API example portion remains official-source-backed; this verification confirms the local handler security caveat and reinforces that agents must inspect configured webhooks before using Lava APIs operationally.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: An Apple TV login menu item can use the login command with page GUIDs for the login, timeout, and success destinations; the login TVML receives single-brace authQrCodeUrl and authCode fields for presenting QR-code or manual-code authentication.
Rock Apple TV is documented as a set-top extension of Rock RMS for TVML applications linked to Rock, and the Apple TV functionality requires Rock version 14 or greater.
Apple TV pages in Rock must output valid TVML and can use Rock-provided Lava merge fields such as CurrentPerson, Context, Campuses, SiteStyles, and CurrentPage.
Apple TV page Lava can inspect the current person's edit and administration access, page parameters, TV shell version, device details, application theme, and whether the client shell is in demo mode.

For Apple TV media playback, supplying an existing watch map sets the resume position; pairing that map with an interaction GUID appends viewing progress to the existing interaction, while omitting the interaction GUID creates a new interaction and watch map beginning from the prior stopping point.

To support sign-in for a Rock Apple TV app without using the TV keyboard, place a Remote Authentication block on an external Rock page, associate the block with the TV application's site, and set that page as the application's authentication page.
MAUI-related Rock Mobile guidance should include styling, border, shadow, animation, toast, and performance behavior because those are visible app-design surfaces, not only build-system concerns.

When building a Rock-linked Apple TV app, use Apple’s TVML documentation for the underlying markup and Rock’s documentation for Rock-specific extensions; modifying the application’s JavaScript is discouraged.
Compatibility support can reduce migration risk by allowing existing Xamarin Forms-style content to run while teams move selected content blocks or pages toward MAUI-native behavior.

A Rock Apple TV page has a cacheability setting: Public permits shared-cache storage, Private limits caching to the client, No-Cache requires revalidation before a local copy is reused, and No-Store prevents local storage for sensitive content.

A TVML text shadow can be specified with horizontal offset, vertical offset, blur radius, and color, but its surrounding element may clip the shadow vertically; keeping the shadow near the text reduces that risk.
Rock Mobile's move toward .NET MAUI should be treated as an evolution from Xamarin Forms rather than an unrelated app platform.
A Rock Apple TV app icon uses three separate image layers for the tvOS parallax effect; foreground layers must be PNG files and the background layer must be a JPG file.
Prepare layered Rock Apple TV app icons at 400×240 pixels for @1x display, 800×480 pixels for @2x display, and 1280×768 pixels for the App Store.

This RockCast episode adds public-safe context for the Rock Mobile transition from Xamarin Forms toward .NET MAUI. It describes MAUI as a close successor with compatibility support, newer styling and animation options, performance improvements, and a release path that lets existing apps test compatibility before fully moving new content blocks to MAUI-native behavior.
